column3: **Request a corrected policy-scope/conflict-surface design and reconcile the duplicate gate for the HOME-search proposal?** Concrete proposal: [role artifact contract](planned/m-fleet-role-artifact-contract.md), frozen SHA df93fee6c072bbdc19850126963049a50ff7df7cd3db13cc573a08e4fd859998. One mandatory revision completed through a quota fallback; final quorum BLOCKED (OpenAI reject, Google pass; both author vendors excluded) and independent MiniMax FAIL/N/A. Remaining premise claims compliance with every standing rule from recipe-only evidence; strict planned-doc duplicate scores1.00/0.95/0.90 remain unresolved. **A (recommended):** request corrected scope-limited policy evidence, inventory/precedence/conflict surface and duplicate-gate reconciliation; a later explicit design approval is still required before planning. **B:** leave current behavior unchanged; ticket stays open. Default if unanswered: B immediately; no planning/execution/merge. No P2 command cap or routing/quota/billing change authorized.

**`skill:idle-record-barred-on-degraded-no-pick-fire` (world, 11-09): narrow Gate 5's idle-record "degraded fire" bar? The design was blocked twice by quorum.** Measured at iteration 97: no product mission has ever promoted an idle fingerprint; World 363–370 never recorded, because every fire fell back somewhere. The bar was a fleet-controller choice (`33190af48`, iteration 91), not a ruling. [Design](planned/m-idle-record-degraded-bar.md): keep the failed-read and unfinished-gate bars, drop the lane-fallback bar, and require each candidate's only unblock event to be a dev-side OPEN ledger flip. Round 2 found two real defects: the proof block ignores the ledger parser's exit status (reproduced by the judge), and no recorded World fire would qualify, because World 370's gates are external predicates, a weekly sweep and a branch-only D-WORLD-113. **A:** one more bounded revision applying every round-2 fix (sol's exit-status capture verbatim; a retro-analysis of the last 10 World and Stapledon no-pick fires, where "do not land" is an acceptable result; a falsifiable observation criterion; a cited no-pick gate list), then one re-quorum, then plan, build and judge. **B (recommended):** no change. On the evidence, the narrowed rule would not have engaged for the mission that filed the ticket. World can make it engage on its own side by recording attended steps as rulings on dev-side ledger rows. The ticket stays open until you rule. Default if unanswered: B. Not HD-2a policy class (judge agrees); this asks because the design failed its gate, not because of policy. **Iteration 127 (measured; recommendation unchanged):** 6 slots lost now, first World 370, latest World 416 and 417. Since `ff08818ae` World's fingerprint `head=` stays on the product commit `0e9e8d35`, so record commits no longer wake it. Every World fire since 2026-11-17 is degraded (codex lane), which bars the record. The bar is not the only blocker, though: a recorded 416 would not have idled 417, because 416 acked its own inbox message (inbox 1 → 0). Of the 8 World fires from 11-19 01:39Z to 11-20 05:39Z, at most 3 could have skipped even if every one had recorded. B's premise was measured on World 370; World 410–417 name the dev-side OPEN rows D-WORLD-119/120 as their gate, the shape the narrowed rule targets. Whether every World candidate's only unblock event is a ledger flip is UNMEASURED. [Judge](fleet-mission-evidence/iteration127/idle-judge.md).

**May the fleet resolve the seven open tickets whose attended fixes merged on 2026-11-16?** Measured at iteration 123: the merges are #2347 → `41c628b94` (`quorum:gpt6-1-sol-openai-api-credits-exhausted`, row 21), #2349 → `005641f82` (`pi:openrouter:uncapped-max-tokens-402`, row 50), #2348 → `509146d24` (`executor:codex-credential-collision-drops-automatic-planner-handoffs`, `executor:codex-credential-lease-collision-fails-concurrent-dispatch`, row 54; `coordinator:job-retry-success-dropped-after-failed-completion`, row 55) and #2343 → `ad2148b23` (`executor:3h-timeout-from-queue-and-unsliced-sprints`, `executor:timeout-loses-work-and-may-never-start`, row 56). It had no queue row; it is now row 68. Under A it is resolved the same way.
